subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class pre-compaction warning, handoff, and bounded deferral lifecycle, and if so which authority and config contract should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes compaction timing, public config, durable checkpoint semantics, and agent authority across a security-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Design Contract First
options.body: Approve a design pass that defines warning thresholds, handoff turn behavior, deferral limits, checkpoint validation, audit logging, and default/upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Notices Only
options.body: Limit this issue to pre-threshold user/agent warnings and leave handoff checkpoints and deferral to separate security-reviewed work.

options.title: Defer New Lifecycle Surface
options.body: Keep current memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoint APIs until a concrete production failure proves that a new deferral mechanism is necessary.

recommendation.title: Design Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve a design pass that defines warning thresholds, handoff turn behavior, deferral limits, checkpoint validation, audit logging, and default/upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for pre-compaction memoryFlush and related product/config ownership points to Peter Steinberger, while checkpoint and notice owners should be consulted for implementation shape.
